sentences: How much do you need to invest each month to be a millionaire by sixty?
Start at twenty, and it's about {£405|four hundred and five pounds} a month.
Let's meet three savers, all aiming for {£1 million|one million pounds} by {60.|sixty.}
Each invests in a Stocks {&|and} Shares ISA, growing at {7%|seven per cent} a year.
Lucy starts at {20,|twenty,} with {£405|four hundred and five pounds} a month.
Tom waits until {30.|thirty.} He needs {£855|eight hundred and fifty five pounds} a month.
Maya starts at {40,|forty,} and needs {£1,970|one thousand nine hundred and seventy pounds} a month.
Every ten years of waiting more than doubles the monthly cost.
Now look at what they actually pay in.
Lucy pays in about {£194,000.|one hundred and ninety four thousand pounds.} Growth does the other {81%.|eighty one per cent.}
Maya pays in {£473,000,|four hundred and seventy three thousand pounds,} and growth does only about half.
But here's the twist. A million pounds in forty years won't buy what it does today.
With {2%|two per cent} inflation, the Bank of England's target, it's worth about {£453,000|four hundred and fifty three thousand pounds} in today's money.
The ISA limit is {£20,000|twenty thousand pounds} a year, about {£1,667|one thousand six hundred and sixty seven pounds} a month, so Maya would need a pension too.
Your turn. Starting at twenty five, how much a month would you need? Comment your guess.
This is an illustration. Investments can fall, and you may get back less.
Starting today? Hit like, and follow for more money maths.
